title: Sowing rocket
subtitle: Cut-and-come-again salad leaves from spring to autumn
excerpt: Rocket is sown direct from March to September in the UK for peppery leaves in three to four weeks. It bolts quickly in hot weather. A short sowing every three weeks in a partly shaded position gives a long season of leaves.
sourceNotes: RHS rocket growing guide (rhs.org.uk). Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), salads chapter. USDA agricultural extension notes on salad greens production, public domain.

glossaryTerms.definition: A related species (Diplotaxis tenuifolia) with narrower, more deeply lobed leaves and a stronger, more persistent peppery flavour than salad rocket (Eruca vesicaria). Wild rocket grows more slowly, bolts less readily in heat, and is more productive as a perennial cut-and-come-again plant. The two types are used interchangeably but are different species.

content.text: Rocket is a peppery salad leaf, ready to cut three to four weeks after sowing in summer. It bolts quickly in warm long days; two small sowings at the start and end of the season outperform a continuous attempt through the summer.
is more heat-tolerant and slower to bolt than salad rocket, and worth growing if you want leaves through July and August.

March through September in the UK. Spring sowings (March to May) and autumn sowings (August to September) are the most productive. A sowing every three weeks gives a rolling harvest rather than a glut. Summer sowings bolt quickly; wild rocket or shading with fleece extends the productive window.

Full sun in spring and autumn; partial shade (north-facing bed, under taller plants) in midsummer to slow bolting. Well-drained, reasonably fertile soil. Rocket grows in containers and window boxes; a pot 15 cm deep with good drainage gives a useful indoor windowsill crop through winter with a grow light, or outdoors through spring.

Sow 0.5 cm deep in shallow drills 15 cm apart. Scatter seed thinly; the plants don't need much space for a cut-and-come-again harvest. Thinning is optional for leaf production; thin to 5 to 8 cm if you want full-sized plants. No transplanting needed: rocket grows quickly from direct seed.

Fast germination: three to five days at 15 to 20°C. The seedlings emerge as two small oval seed leaves. Germination is reliable across a wide temperature range (5 to 25°C). Very hot dry soil can inhibit germination in July; water the drill before sowing.

Cut the leaves when plants are 8 to 10 cm tall, 3 cm above the ground, and let them regrow for a second and third cut. Water consistently; drought accelerates bolting and makes the flavour very sharp. Once the plant produces a central flower stem, the leaves become too hot and fibrous to eat in quantity; compost the plant and resow.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: Rocket is a quick crop with few serious problems.

items.symptom: Leaves very hot and bitter after the first cut
items.fix: Water consistently. Cut back any flower stems as they form. Sow wild rocket for a milder, more heat-tolerant crop in summer.

items.cause: Flea beetle (Phyllotreta species), the main rocket pest.
items.fix: Cover with fine insect-proof mesh from sowing onwards. Flea beetle damage is cosmetic on rocket; a light infestation doesn't prevent harvest.

items.symptom: Plant bolts in the first two weeks after germination
items.cause: Sown during long days in June or July in full sun.
items.fix: Sow in partial shade for summer sowings. Use wild rocket. Wait until August for the next outdoor sowing.
